//: Complete check set for four Makerfabs AgroSense devices: AGLWSM02, AGLWTH01, AGLWPP01, AGLWL01. Derived from their normalized codec manifests in @intelligent-farming/lorawan-codec-normalization — every path below is verified against that codec's decoded output, not inferred from the model name.
//devices: AGLWL01  → codec makerfabs/light-intensity   → battery(V), air.lightIntensity(lux), seqNo
AGLWPP01 → codec makerfabs/pipe-pressure     → battery(V), pressure.gauge(kPa), sampleCount, reportingInterval
AGLWTH01 → codec makerfabs/air-temperature-and-humidity (also ath20 / temperature-humidity-sht31 — identical output) → battery(V), air.temperature(C), air.relativeHumidity(%)
AGLWSM02 → codec makerfabs/soil-monitor      → battery(V), soil.moisture(%), soil.temperature(C), soil.ec(dS/m), soil.pH, transmitInterval
AGLWSM02 alt → codec makerfabs/soil-moisture → battery(V), soilMoistureAdc (UNCALIBRATED raw count, not a percentage)
//model-mapping: Only AGLWL01 is stamped in the codec source (light-intensity/codec.js). The other three are mapped by the AGLW<abbrev><version> convention: PP=Pipe Pressure, TH=Temperature/Humidity, SM=Soil Moisture. TH01 is safe either way — all three Makerfabs climate codecs emit identical paths. SM02 is the one to confirm: makerfabs/soil-monitor emits normalized soil.* fields, while makerfabs/soil-moisture emits only an uncalibrated soilMoistureAdc count. Both variants are configured below; delete the block that does not apply. Confirm with:  SELECT DISTINCT device_profile_name, jsonb_pretty(object) FROM event_up WHERE device_profile_name ILIKE '%soil%' ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 5;
//profiles: deviceProfiles values must match your ChirpStack device_profile_name exactly. The names below are placeholders — list yours with:  SELECT DISTINCT device_profile_name, count(*) FROM event_up GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
//thresholds: Thresholds are starting points in the vocabulary's guaranteed units (C, %, kPa, lux, V, dS/m). Battery figures especially need calibration against your own fleet — these devices do not share a voltage range. Establish yours with:  SELECT device_profile_name, min((object->>'battery')::numeric), percentile_cont(0.05) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (object->>'battery')::numeric), max((object->>'battery')::numeric) FROM event_up WHERE object ? 'battery' GROUP BY 1;

checks.//: ════════ FLEET-WIDE, SCOPED PER DEVICE FAMILY ════════ These are the checks where the candidate path does NOT scope the check for you, because every device emits the field. battery is the clearest case: a coin-cell light sensor and a pipe-pressure logger do not share a low-battery voltage, so one fleet-wide threshold either cries wolf on one or stays silent on the other.
Soil monitor: 4-in-1 probe, typically a larger pack. Confirm against your fleet.
Pipe pressure runs a higher supply (its vectors span 3.6–4.0 V), so a 3.2 V raise point would never fire before the node died.
Light sensor sits lowest of the four — its vectors show normal operation at 2.9 V. The fleet default of 3.4 V would alert on a healthy device immediately.
Silence, scoped by family because reporting intervals differ. Pipe pressure defaults to 300–1800 s; the soil monitor reports on transmitInterval (hours). A single threshold cannot suit both.
Codec producing nothing. Unscoped on purpose — you want this on any device, including one whose profile you have not listed here.

════════ AGLWSM02 — SOIL MONITOR ════════ soil.moisture(%), soil.temperature(C), soil.ec(dS/m), soil.pH. These four paths are emitted by nothing else in the fleet, so the checks below need no deviceProfiles — the candidate path IS the scope.
Waterlogging: root-zone oxygen loss after over-irrigation or heavy rain.
Moisture falling fast after irrigation means the water went somewhere other than the root zone — a broken line, or drainage far quicker than the soil type suggests.
A probe lifted out of the ground keeps reporting a plausible constant forever. Invisible to every threshold above.
Root-zone frost. Separate from air frost: soil lags air by hours, so this is the one that tells you the roots were actually hit.
Salinity. soil.ec is dS/m; above ~4 is a yield problem for most crops. Rising EC with falling moisture is the fertiliser-burn signature.
EC climbing steadily means salts accumulating — usually irrigation water quality or insufficient leaching.
pH band. Widen for your crop — blueberries and brassicas want very different windows.
One probe element failing while the others keep reporting — the field vanishes from the codec output and every check above it goes quiet. Silence looks identical to health, which is why this matters.

════════ AGLWSM02 — RAW-ADC VARIANT ════════ Only if your SM02 resolves to makerfabs/soil-moisture, which emits soilMoistureAdc instead of soil.*. That value is an UNCALIBRATED capacitive count (the codec attaches a warning saying so), not a percentage — the thresholds below are raw counts and MUST be calibrated per probe and soil type. Observed vector range is roughly 1500–2048. Delete this block if your SM02 is the 4-in-1 soil-monitor.
Higher ADC count generally means drier on capacitive probes, but verify the direction on your hardware before trusting it — some invert.
Works without calibration: a raw count that never moves is a detached or failed probe regardless of what the number means.
Also calibration-free: a hard rail at 0 or full-scale means an open or shorted probe lead.

════════ AGLWTH01 — AIR TEMPERATURE & HUMIDITY ════════ air.temperature(C), air.relativeHumidity(%). Note the candidate lists include bare `temperature` so these entries keep working if you add a plain temperature probe (e.g. makerfabs/rtd-pt1000-temperature) later.
Current air frost risk.
Did it frost overnight, even though the morning reading has recovered? Uses the window MINIMUM, so the event is not erased by daybreak.
Falling 3 C/h at dusk is the shape of a frost event hours before the temperature itself is alarming. This is the entry that buys you time to act.

Sustained high humidity is the primary driver of fungal infection periods. Leadsman cannot compute a dew point (it has no derived-value support), so this plus th01-temperature-crash is the practical approximation.
Very low humidity — transpiration stress under glass, or a failed humidifier.
A saturated or failed RH element pins at exactly 100 % (or 0) and stops moving. Threshold checks are satisfied; the reading is junk.
Air temperature is the least likely reading to be genuinely constant over a day, which makes a frozen value strong evidence of a failed sensor.

════════ AGLWPP01 — PIPE PRESSURE ════════ pressure.gauge(kPa). The most operationally valuable of the four for irrigation: pressure tells you whether the system is actually doing what you commanded. 100 kPa ≈ 14.5 psi ≈ 1 bar.
Line pressure lost while it should be running: pump failed, well ran dry, or the main broke. Critical — irrigation is silently not happening.
Overpressure: a closed valve downstream, a blockage, or a failed regulator. Risks bursting the weakest fitting.
A sudden sustained drop is a burst or a sheared fitting. Catches it while pressure is still nominally in band, which is hours before the tank empties.
Climbing fast usually means a valve closed against a running pump (deadhead) — expensive for the pump.
Water hammer. A transient spike between uplinks that averages away completely — only the window MAXIMUM sees it.
A failed transducer or a blocked sensing port reads a constant. Every threshold above stays satisfied while the pressure reading is meaningless.

════════ AGLWL01 — LIGHT INTENSITY ════════ air.lightIntensity(lux). The awkward one: lux spans five orders of magnitude between night and noon, so a plain low-light threshold would fire every single evening. Use the daily PEAK instead — that is what distinguishes a fouled sensor from nightfall.

The important entry. A daily maximum that never gets bright means the sensor is dirty, obscured by canopy growth, snow-covered, or buried — not that it was dark. This is measurement-peak's max/below combination, which a threshold check cannot express.
A photodiode reading exactly 0 around the clock is a dead element or a disconnected head — distinct from 'dim', and worth escalating.
A latched ADC produces a constant across day and night, which no real light sensor does.

Supplemental-lighting check for a greenhouse: if the daily peak never reaches the crop's requirement, the lamps are not compensating. Set the threshold from your DLI target and enable only under glass.

════════ LINK QUALITY (all four) ════════ Unscoped: RSSI has nothing to do with which sensor is attached. Disabled until you have tuned the threshold to your gateway layout, or it will be noisy on the first run.
